title: The Model Gives the 6-1 HULK a 5% Chance, and Second Place Goes on the Line in Philly's House
dek: Week 8 brings a 5-2 showdown at the top, a first-place team the numbers have left for dead, and three 3-4 or worse squads fighting for their playoff lives.
body: Welcome to the week 8 pregame, and we open in Team Pillbert's building, where Philly hosts Sonny with both teams at 5-2 and second place on the line. The model has picked a side, and it isn't the home team: The Horse is Hea is a 74% favorite, with 853.6 points for to Team Pillbert's 817.8 and title odds of 29% to 12%. The all-time series couldn't be tighter at Alan 5-6 Sonny, and the week 1 meeting went to the Horse by just 106.42 to 102.1. This is also the first start for Christian Watson and Ashton Jeanty in Horse colors, so Sonny's new trade haul goes straight into the biggest game of the week.

The Ones to Watch tell you how steep the climb is for Philly. Jahmyr Gibbs, his No. 2 overall pick, can drop 32 or more and Team Pillbert only gets to 49%, a coin flip; if Gibbs goes under 10, the home side sinks to 11%. On the other side, a 25-point day from Jaxon Smith-Njigba pushes the Horse to 87%, and even a dud under 8 still leaves Sonny a 62% favorite. Alan's playoff odds sit at 79% to the Horse's 93%, so a loss here won't end anything, but it would hand the stable a clear path to the No. 2 seed.

Now the number that made the whole studio do a double take. Ramon's No Banner only HULK is 6-1, riding a three-game streak, leads the league with 927.4 points for and holds 98% playoff odds, and the model gives Brucie a 5% chance to beat Mekhi's 2-5 Dawgs. Whatever it is seeing in Sunday's lineups, it is seeing a lot: Ja'Marr Chase going for 27 or more makes the Dawgs a 99% favorite, and a Chase stinker under 7 still leaves Kai at 89%. Kenneth Walker III scoring 25-plus only lifts the HULK to 11%. Ramon leads the series 6-3 and won the week 1 meeting 177.86 to 98.36, but Kai debuts James Cook III and Jameson Williams with the numbers firmly in his corner.

Habib and Z² meet as 3-4 teams that both won last week, and it is closer to an elimination game than either record admits. The Habibsters are 75% favorites with 797.8 points for against Ghostu-Spider SZN's 660.4, and a Puka Nacua game of 27 or more pushes Kaushal to 89%. But Zoey already owns this matchup, winning 129.56 to 108.6 in week 1, and she brings a Jordan Love and Tucker Kraft stack, which is the most Wisconsin sentence in this preview. Tetairoa McMillan is her swing piece: 20-plus gets her to 42%, under 4 drops her to 13%, and with playoff odds of 48% for Habib and 19% for Zoe, the loser has a long winter ahead.

Finally, Randy brings a four-game skid to JMoney's place, and The fumblers are 76% favorites to end it. Randy won the week 1 meeting 146.16 to 75.96, and a Derrick Henry game of 26-plus makes it 92%, though after Henry's last two weeks a sub-8 line, which leaves Randy at 59%, is not unthinkable. Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland form the fumblers' stack, and Jordan's hope runs through Joe Burrow, the league's top scorer last week: 28 or more gets Counting or not Counting GV to 40%, under 15 drops it to 10%. At 33% playoff odds, Randy needs this one; at 1%, Jordan just wants to ruin his week.

social.author: Sal Benedetto
social.text: Everybody's 0-0 on the panel and I'm about to be 4-0. The Horse is a LOCK. The HULK is a LOCK. 5%?? The 6-1 team?? I'll take that action every day and twice in the playoffs. 🔒🔒

social.author: Dr. Nina Kessler
social.text: Dawgs at 95%. Even if Ja'Marr Chase scores under 7, the model still has them at 89%. I don't call many locks, but I'm calling this one. Sal, please hedge.

social.author: No Banner only HULK
social.text: MATCHDAY: No Banner only HULK hosts Dawgs. 💚 6-1, three straight wins, 927.4 points for. The numbers say 5%. We say see you Sunday.

social.author: Dawg Pound Dre
social.text: Nina calling a LOCK on the Dawgs is the nicest thing anyone has said about us all year. Cook and Williams debut against the leader and we're 95% favorites. Bark louder. 🐾

social.author: Pill Brigade Pete
social.text: Nina has us at 26% and Dana 'leans' Horse like that's polite. Marcus is the only one on this panel who remembers the week 1 game was decided by 4.32. Philly at home. Sit down. 💊

social.author: Midwest Mel
social.text: Sal picking Ghostu-Spider SZN with his whole chest and Nina still treating us like a 25% rounding error. Love to Kraft on a Sunday, Zoey already beat Habib once. Spin the web. 🕷️

social.author: Counting Crew Carla
social.text: Marcus said we'd score 70 again. Thanks, Marcus. Burrow needs 28 for a 40% chance. That's the most hope this team has had since week 1. 🎺

picks.game: Team Pillbert (Alan) vs The Horse is Hea (Sonny)

panel.take: Watson and Jeanty get their first start for Sonny, and that lineup is deeper than it was a week ago. Philly is 5-2 for a reason, so I'll keep this to a lean.
This series is 5-6, the last meeting was decided by 4.32, and the home team is being handed 26% like a consolation prize. Rivalries this even don't care about trade grades; Philly holds serve.
LOCK IT UP. JSN under 8 and they're STILL 62%? That's not a pick, that's a deposit.
74% for the Horse, and the Gibbs line says it all: 32 points only gets Team Pillbert to 49%. Marcus is welcome to the other 26%.
Kaushal has been working the wire hard and it's showing on the scoreboard, two straight wins. 797.8 points for against 660.4 is a real gap.

The rookie owns the head-to-head and has already toppled two contenders, which is exactly the kind of story I'd normally ride. But a two-time champion at 48% playoff odds is a dangerous animal, and I'm siding with the history of the trophy.
She beat him by 21 in week 1 and she's got a Packers stack going. I don't fade hot rookies, I MARRY them. LOCK.
75% for Kaushal, and a Puka game of 27-plus pushes it to 89%. Sal is picking the week 1 box score, not this one.

picks.game: Counting or not Counting GV (Jordan) vs The fumblers (Randy)

panel.take: Randy turned over half the roster after last week, so this is a new-look lineup chasing a skid-ender. Against a 1-6 team, it should be enough.
Four-game losing streaks end one of two ways: against a team like this, or in total collapse. I'll trust the 146-point week 1 performance over the last month, but only barely.
Caleb and Loveland on the same roster against a team that scored 60 last week? LOCK. Henry owes everybody, and he's paying this week.
76% for The fumblers. Henry under 8 still leaves them at 59%, which matters, given his last two weeks. Jordan's path is Burrow at 28-plus, and even that's only 40%.

picks.game: No Banner only HULK (Ramon) vs Dawgs (Mekhi)

panel.take: A 5% number for a 6-1 team tells me the model sees something in Sunday's lineups. I'd want to see what Ramon sets before I go further than a lean, but Kai has the numbers.
The best team in the league, 6-3 in the series, at home, and the model says 5%? I've built a career on picks like this. Somebody has to stand with the leader.
927.4 POINTS. 177 in the last meeting. I don't care what the computer had for breakfast, this is the biggest LOCK of the year.
95% for the Dawgs, and Chase under 7 still leaves them at 89%. Walker scoring 25-plus only gets the HULK to 11%. This is my one lock, and Sal and Marcus are on the 5% side.
